title: Empirical Formula and Molecular Formula Calculation

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

expression: n = (molecular formula mass) / (empirical formula mass)  ;  Molecular formula = n × (Empirical formula)
explanation: Empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound, found by converting percentage composition (or mass) of each element to moles, then dividing by the smallest mole value to get a simple ratio. Molecular formula is the ACTUAL number of atoms, always a whole-number multiple (n) of the empirical formula, found by dividing the compound's true molar mass by the empirical formula's mass.

variables.meaning: Whole-number multiple relating empirical to molecular formula

workedExample.scenario: A compound is 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O by mass, with molar mass ≈ 180 g/mol.
workedExample.substitution: Moles: C = 40/12 = 3.33, H = 6.7/1 = 6.7, O = 53.3/16 = 3.33. Ratio C:H:O = 1:2:1, empirical formula CH₂O (mass 30). n = 180/30 = 6

commonMistakes: Stopping at the empirical formula and presenting it as the final molecular formula without checking against the given molar mass — the two are only the same when n = 1.
Rounding mole ratios incorrectly to the nearest whole number too early — small ratios like 1.5 should be doubled (to 3) rather than rounded to 2 or 1, to get true whole-number ratios.
genZNote: Empirical formula is the simplified 'summary' — molecular formula is the actual, full-length version.
